general_information.Description: The Capptone Project provides students, working in groups (each group consists of 4-5 students), with a significant project experience in which they can integrate much of the material they have learned in their program, including matters relating to requirements, design, human factors, professionalism, and project management. Students will be guided to Develop an IA solution, employing knowledge gained from courses throughout the program. It includes development of risk assessement, analysis and management, implementation, and quality assurance. Students may follow any suitable process model, must pay attention to quality issues, and must manage the project themselves, following all appropriate project management techniques. Success of the project is determined in large part by whether students have adequately solved their customer’s problem.
general_information.StudentTasks: # Choose project at project market and form group. # Divide and schedule work among members # Attend all scheduled meeting with supervisor. # Produce document and product according to project requirement and member work share. # Defence work infront of examination board, showing both project results and individual responsibility # Students are required to attend at least 80% of scheduled meetings with their supervisor(s) to be eligible for the thesis or capstone defense.
general_information.Tools: Appropriate tools for design and implementation.
general_information.Note: 1) On-going Assessment - Project documents: 50% 2) Final Project Presentation: 50% 3) Final Result: 100% Completion Criteria: 1) Every on-going assessment component >0 2) On-going assessment: 4 reports, after 6 weeks >=5 3) On-going assessment >=5 4) Project Defense >=4 5) Final Result >=5

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Use acquired knowledge to identify a problem requiring technological intervention and specify requirements for the proposed solution and algorithm.
Collect data under techical & other factors.
Apply project management principles to IA projects
Practice oral presentation and inter-personal communications

assessments.Grading Guide: • Based on Group Mark (GM). Each group on every stage (with report) will be evaluated by its supervisor. This evaluation is called continuous assessment. • Personal Mark (in range: from 0% to 120%GM) will also be given for all Reports or all continuous assessment. • Every on-going assessment component >0 • On-going assessment: 4 reports, after 6 weeks >=5 • On-going assessment >=5
assessments.Note: 50% of Final CP Mark with weight (On-going assessment) - Report No. 1: 5% - Report No. 2: 10% - Report No. 3: 25% - Report No. 4: 25% - Report No. 5: 25% - Report No. 6: 10%

assessments.Grading Guide: • Presentation mark is given by each member of referee committee for each student on final project presentation. This personal mark is the average of all member of referee committee.
assessments.Note: • Final Project Result = On-going assessment (6 Reports) x 50% + Defense Mark (by Committee) x 50%
